chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man bequeathed thirty dinars for the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her). He said: So the man brought it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it to so-and-so, an elder from the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her), and he was a breadwinner with scarcity (of means).'

The man said to him: 'But rather, the man bequeathed it for the children of Fatimah.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, it does not fall upon the (general) children of Fatimah, and it falls upon this man (who is among them), and for him are dependants.'

key_terms.عِيَالٌ: Dependants/those supported by the head of household
key_terms.وُلْدِ فَاطِمَةَ: Children of Fatimah (descendants of the Prophet's daughter)

ai.seo_question: How do Shia jurists interpret the term 'children of Fatimah' in inheritance and bequest contexts?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the principle of *al-wasiyyah li-man awsiya lahu* (the bequest goes to the specific person intended by the testator) by directing funds to a specific poor descendant of Fatimah (AS) rather than the general group. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on *maqasid* (objectives) and *maslaha* (public interest), where the welfare of the needy takes precedence over rigid literal interpretation of the category 'children of Fatimah'.
